utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case IT-06-90-A, the Prosecutor versus Gotovina and Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me start by ensuring that all the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Gotovina, I wanted to make sure that you can hear the proceedings in a language that you understand. THE APPELLANT GOTOVINA: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gotovina. Mr. Markac. Can you hear -- THE APPELLANT MARKAC: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Markac. Appearances of the parties. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Ingrid Elliott for the Prosecution. I'm joined today by Senior Prosecution Counsel Helen Brady, Senior Appeals Counsel Douglas Stringer, and our Case Manager Lourdes Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thanks. Just one second. There's one technical problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll manage this time without it. Registrar, would you make sure that in the future the computer is properly adjusted from one case to another before I come in. Thank you. So we'll just proceed without that. Counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Gregory Kehoe for General Gotovina, along with Luka Misetic to my right, and to my far right, Mr. Guenael Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, everyone in the courtroom. My name is Goran Mikulicic. On my left side is Mr. Tom Kuzmanovic and Mr. John Jones, and on my right side is Mr. Vlado Rendulic, our Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. As you're all aware, Rule --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: As you're all aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the appellants to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained person. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 29 September 2011. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order issued on 6 January 2012. I would like to begin this Status Conference inquiring into Mr. Gotovina's and Mr. Markac's health. If either Mr. Gotovina or Mr. Markac would prefer this discussion to take place in closed session, that will be fine with me. Is there any need to close the session, Mr. Gotovina? THE APPELLANT GOTOVINA: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour, but it's all right. There is no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So we can proceed with an open session. THE APPELLANT GOTOVINA: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So, I hope you have been well, Mr. Gotovina, and there are no problems with regard to your physical well-being or mental well-being. THE APPELLANT GOTOVINA: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour. I am all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gotovina. Mr. Markac, the same question, you have been well, I hope. THE APPELLANT MARKAC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my condition is not good and currently the medical service at the Detention Unit is taking adequate measures. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope you will be better, and that if you are sick, I will be informed. Now, let me turn to an update of the procedural history of this case. Currently there are a number of pending motions and applications. On 4 November 2011, counsel for Mr. Gotovina filed the public redacted version of Appellant Ante Gotovina's motion to admit new evidence pursuant to Rule 115. On 13 January 2012, the Appeals Chamber received the application and proposed amicus curiae brief concerning the 15 April 2011 Trial Chamber judgement and requesting that the Appeals Chamber consider the findings of unlawful artillery attacks during Operation Storm. These motions will be decided in due course. In addition to the motions just mentioned, there are a number of confidential motions currently pending. These motions will also be decided in due course. I take this opportunity to inform the parties that the appeals hearing in this case will likely take place in the spring. Once the date for the hearing has been set, a Scheduling Order will be issued. At this point I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: No issues by the Prosecution to raise. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Nothing as well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for attending this meeting, and since there are no other matters to be raised, I will simply thank everybody for your attendance and call the proceedings to a close. The Court will rise.
